summary: Defines a way to write GeoJSON as a sequence of separate items, with the media type application/geo+json-seq. It builds on JSON text sequences so very large geographic datasets can be read piece by piece instead of all at once.

eli5.summary: Rather than one huge map folded into a giant sheet, you get a stack of small cards. You can read them one at a time.

questions: how to stream large geojson files
what is a geojson text sequence
why use record separator in geojson
subtitle: A way to write huge GeoJSON datasets as a stream of small, separately parsable items.

tldr.problem: Geographic datasets can hold tens of thousands or millions of features, and a single GeoJSON document has to be read as a whole.
tldr.mechanism: A GeoJSON text sequence is any number of GeoJSON texts, each preceded by an ASCII record separator (RS) character and followed by a line feed (LF), following the JSON text sequence rules.
tldr.outcome: Datasets of arbitrary size can be produced and parsed incrementally. The media type is application/geo+json-seq.

today: RFC 8142 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Sequences
sections.content:
Very large sequences of values are a problem for JSON, as explained in the motivation for JSON text sequences (RFC 7464). GeoJSON has the same problem: geographic datasets often run to the tens of thousands or millions of features, and big arrays of coordinates make it worse.

RFC 8142 specializes JSON text sequences. A GeoJSON text sequence is a document of arbitrary size holding one or more GeoJSON objects, not just a single FeatureCollection, Feature or Geometry.
sections.eli5: A map with millions of places is too big to read in one go. This lets you split it into many small pieces.

sections.title: The Sequence Format
sections.content:
A GeoJSON text sequence is any number of GeoJSON texts, each encoded in UTF-8, preceded by one ASCII record separator (RS) character and followed by a line feed (LF). It follows all the rules of RFC 7464 and adds one constraint: each JSON text MUST contain a single GeoJSON object.

Mixed sequences of Geometry, Feature and FeatureCollection objects are permitted. How producers and parsers agree on which GeoJSON types are allowed in a given exchange is not specified.
sections.eli5: Each card starts with a special marker and ends with a line break, and each card holds one place or shape.

sections.title: Interoperability Advice
sections.content:
Using the RS character 0x1e to mark each text means producers and parsers need not enforce a canonical form: any valid GeoJSON, pretty-printed or compact, can be used.

Many deployed parsers are built for newline-delimited sequences of compact JSON. Sequences of compact GeoJSON texts with no internal newlines are more interoperable with them. Where ordering and exactly-once delivery are hard to achieve, sequences that do not depend on the order of texts are more interoperable.
sections.eli5: Short cards with no line breaks inside are easiest for other people's card readers. It also helps if the order of the cards does not matter.

sections.title: Media Type and Security
sections.content:
IANA registered the media type application/geo+json-seq, which uses the suffix established in RFC 8091. Its encoding considerations are listed as binary, and its intended usage is COMMON.

GeoJSON text sequences have no security considerations beyond those of JSON text sequences and the GeoJSON format.
sections.eli5: The format gets its own official label so programs know what is in the file. It adds no new safety worries.
